independent_variables.definition: Simulated stock returns over the same 12-month window, generated from full-sample return-on-earnings coefficients, firm i’s earnings, and a randomly selected full-sample regression error term for firm k in the same year, without replacement.
independent_variables.formula: Rit_sim = β0_full + β1_full * Xit + τkt, where τkt is sampled without replacement from firm k residuals in the same year.

evidence.quote: Rit is the (actual or simulated) return over the 12-month period beginning nine months prior to the end of the fiscal year.
We match the earnings of firm i during year t with a randomly selected (without replacement) error term of firm k during year t.
We use the earnings of firm i during year t and the randomly matched error term to generate a simulated stock return using the previously estimated intercept and slope coefficients for firm i.

presents statistics for the sample replicating Basu (1997) covering the sample period 1963–1990.
Panel B presents statistics for the sample period 1991–2001. Panel C presents statistics for alternative analysis conducted also using the sample period 1963–1990. Rit is stock returns for firm i over
the 12-month period beginning nine months prior to fiscal year-end, with ‘‘Actual’’ referring to
actual returns, and ‘‘Simulated’’ referring to simulated returns generated as discussed in Table 2.
Xit represents earnings before extraordinary items and discontinued operations for fiscal year t,
scaled by stock price nine months prior to fiscal year-end. Eit is earnings before extraordinary items
and discontinued operations for year t. MVEit-1 is the market value of equity at the beginning of
